description:
The schema's per-command success types come from the handler registry instead of a hand-kept match table, so every visible command names its typed response.

## Background

`get_output_schema_for_command(cmd_path)` in `crates/jit/src/schema.rs` matches `"group_sub"` strings to `schema_for!(T)` and falls back to `(None, "CommandResponse")`. The table has drifted: its `"graph_downstream"` key matches no path (`downstream` is only an alias of `graph rdeps`), so `graph rdeps` and `rdeps` report `CommandResponse` although they emit `GraphDownstreamResponse`. Command groups now run as library handlers in `crates/jit/src/dispatch/`, one module per group, each returning `anyhow::Result<Outcome<R>>` with `R` its registered response type, and one registration per group generates both dispatch and a per-leaf response lookup. During migration `generate()` consulted the registry first and the table second. `CommandSchema::generate()` must remain the derivation authority with `get_output_schema_for_command`, `hidden_commands()` and `builtin_global_flags()` reachable from it. Clap-hidden items are already excluded from the schema.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: `get_output_schema_for_command` remains reachable from `generate()` and answers only from the handler registry; its hand-written path-to-type table no longer exists.
- [hard] REQ-02: No executable command path in the generated schema reports `CommandResponse` as its success type.
- [hard] REQ-03: A schema test walks the visible executable paths of `Cli::command()` and fails when any has no registered response.
- [hard] REQ-04: Commands whose schema output changes from `CommandResponse` to a typed response, `graph rdeps` among them, are covered by a schema test stating the typed response, and existing schema suites pass without weakened assertions.
- [hard] REQ-05: MCP tool generation and its unit and integration tests pass against the regenerated schema.
